findings.what: HTML injection via unescaped RPC-derived strings into innerHTML: line 321 interpolates String(e.message) (can be j.error.message from any configured RPC endpoint) and lines 350-356 interpolate dgpo.head_block_id/time/current_supply etc. directly into innerHTML. docs CSP has no form-action directive.
findings.why: A hostile/compromised community RPC endpoint (api.justyy.com, steem.61bts.com, api.deathwing.me are community-run) can inject arbitrary HTML into the trusted cockpit page. script-src 'self' blocks script execution, but form-action is unset and per CSP3 does NOT fall back to default-src — an injected overlay (position:fixed) with a fake 're-enter password' form can submit the master password cross-origin. The master password opens BOTH gates (shared canon-62 wrap), so this is a credible phishing primitive against the single most valuable secret. Impact is phishing-grade (requires operator re-typing), not script-execution grade — stated honestly.
findings.fix: Render error/state strings via textContent or the existing escapeHtml() instead of innerHTML interpolation (lines 321, 350-356, and apply the same discipline to renderCustody/renderAudit for vault-derived strings); add form-action 'none' to docs/index.html CSP.

findings.what: Army-vault zip password (keysZipPass) is read in plaintext from recovery-meta.json which lives in the same external steem repo as the encrypted KEYS-ZIP…ROT4.zip.enc.
findings.why: Double sha256 pins prove integrity, not confidentiality. If the steem repo is public (or any reader is compromised), anyone can decrypt all 15 accounts' WIFs (owner/active/posting/memo). The design 'new machine + one credential (PAT)' confirms the password is not treated as a secret. Unverifiable from this clone — severity escalates to C if that repo is world-readable.
findings.fix: Do not ship the vault password inside the repo that holds the ciphertext: keep keysZipPass out of recovery-meta.json (operator-provided at unseal time or derived from a secret held outside both repos); at minimum verify the steem repo is private and plan a key rotation round (worklog already flags 61 stale keys).

findings.what: verify.sh copies /tmp/gate-crypto.js → /tmp/gate-crypto-verify.cjs and requires it as code, and auto-selects the work dir via `ls -dt /tmp/sovereign-* | head -1`.
findings.why: /tmp is world-writable (sticky bit): on a multi-user host another local user can pre-plant gate-crypto.js (bootstrap itself never creates it; whoever does controls key-derivation code of the custody audit) or pre-create a decoy /tmp/sovereign-* dir that verify.sh then treats as the sovereign work dir. Single-operator machines make this low-probability, but the script's whole point is distrust.
findings.fix: Keep the crypto file inside the clone (e.g., reference $WORK/Sandbox/docs/vendor/gate-crypto.js) and take WORK from an env var written by bootstrap.sh instead of ls -dt.

findings.what: No clickjacking defense on either gate: frame-ancestors absent (and cannot be delivered via <meta> per CSP spec; GitHub Pages cannot set HTTP headers) and no JS framebusting; cockpit has confirm()-less broadcast buttons (claimOne, claim-all).
findings.why: Both pages can be iframed and click-shadowed. Impact: forced chain actions (claims — benign; votes/follows — manipulable; op-send is protected by a native confirm() dialog the framing cannot fake). No secret disclosure (key-reveal renders only to the victim's own screen).
findings.fix: Add JS framebust on both gates (if (window.top !== window.self) document.documentElement.style.display='none' + a visible warning) and optionally a confirm() before every broadcast including claims.

findings.what: Console CSP uses script-src 'unsafe-inline' and style-src 'unsafe-inline' (single-file architecture), weaker than the cockpit's script-src 'self'.
findings.why: Defense-in-depth gap only: the console has no dynamic HTML sinks today (render() is textContent-only, verified) and connect-src 'self', so nothing is exploitable now — but any future innerHTML mistake would become full XSS.
findings.fix: Extract the script/style into console/app.js + console/style.css and switch to script-src 'self' (mirror the cockpit).

findings.what: renderOpsFields() builds form HTML via string templates with unescaped value="${val}" and <textarea>${val}</textarea>.
findings.why: All current call sites pass static empty/constant values, so it is safe today; the pattern is one refactor away from attribute injection if any field is ever prefilled from dynamic data (prefillClaim writes via .value, which is safe).
findings.fix: Build fields with createElement/setAttribute, or route val/ph through escapeHtml() before interpolation.

findings.what: Dead node heredoc: `node - "$VAULT" <<'JS' … require("file:///tmp/gate-crypto-verify.mjs") … JS` always throws (missing file / ESM-via-require) and exits 1 with a stack trace; the real audit is the following block.
findings.why: No direct security impact (script continues, no set -e), but it is confusing noise and its failure looks like an audit step.
findings.fix: Delete the dead heredoc block.

findings.what: Cockpit claims 'lock wipes everything' but lock() only nulls references; WIFs and decrypted payload persist in JS strings until GC, and JS cannot zero string memory.
findings.why: Best-effort only — same limitation seal.mjs documents honestly ('שאריות-מחרוזת-ב-JS-מתועדות-כמקובל'). Residual memory risk to a local forensic attacker is inherent to JS; the docs overstate the guarantee.
findings.fix: State the GC caveat in README/SECURITY wording for the cockpit; keep nulling (it is still correct practice).

findings.what: No name-based patterns for credential files: upload/ and .passfile are covered, but bootstrap.sh also probes $PWD/upload/pat.env and $HOME/upload/pat.env, and fleet-vault keys.env conventions exist; *.env / pat.env / keys.env are not ignored.
findings.why: One mkdir/rename away from staging a PAT file outside the covered paths.
findings.fix: Add: *.env, pat.env, keys.env, *.passfile.

findings.what: Pattern set has no PEM private-key block (-----BEGIN), no AWS AKIA, no generic bot/api-key shapes; --passfile needle matches only the exact trimmed bytes of the passfile (a derived/canon form of the same secret would not match).
findings.why: The repo's own threat-model classes (WIF, GitHub tokens, cred-URLs, machine paths) are covered and fail-closed is verified live, but adjacent secret formats pass silently; passfile matching is exact-match, not secret-family match.
findings.fix: Add PEM/AWS patterns; document the exact-match limitation of --passfile next to the usage string.

findings.what: The public gate displays a hint naming the operator's real password file: 'headcorner.txt — הסיסמה הראשית…'.
findings.why: SECURITY.md's own console law is 'no hints' (לא-רמז); the cockpit violates it cosmetically. Value to an attacker is small (a filename), but it is inconsistent doctrine and aids targeted phishing lures.
findings.fix: Replace with a neutral hint (accepted password formats) or none.

findings.what: Vendored crypto carries no in-repo integrity pin (no sha256 comment, no provenance record); the 'verbatim copy of SovereignConsole' claim cannot be checked from this clone.
findings.why: It is first-party code (not a CDN lib) and its ECDSA was live-verified (verify_authority=TRUE per worklog), but nothing in-repo lets a future reviewer detect silent drift from the audited source.
findings.fix: Add a header comment with the file's sha256 + the SovereignConsole source path/commit it was copied from, and a one-line diff command to re-verify.

findings.what: RUNBOOK instructs `shred -u .passfile` as the credential-erasure step.
findings.why: shred gives weak guarantees on journaled filesystems/SSDs (copy-on-write, wear leveling). Mitigated: the password is only ever copied to .passfile transiently and seal.mjs holds it in memory; residual risk is the on-disk temp copy itself.
findings.fix: Prefer creating the passfile on tmpfs (/dev/shm, mode 600) and unlinking; note the shred caveat honestly.

findings.what:
Untracked WIP receipt (agent-3d) contains a personal machine path — leak-scan correctly BLOCKS it. Verbatim failure output:
[leak-scan] ✖ workpath · receipts/browser-verify-t42.md:7 (תוכן-לא-מודפס)
[leak-scan] נחסם: 1 התאמות — אסור-לדחוף. תקן-מקור, לא-רק-את-הסריקה.
findings.why: The gate did its job (fail-closed before push); if the protocol is followed nothing leaks. Reported because the task requires verbatim reporting of any leak-scan failure, and the file must be fixed before staging.
findings.fix: Replace the absolute path on line 7 with a repo-relative path ('receipts/browser-verify-t42.json') before committing; the JSON twin (browser-verify-t42.json) is clean and scan-passes.

findings.what: Crypto parameters byte-verified: console = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 ×650,000 (≥600k ✓), AES-256-GCM tag 128-bit ✓, salt 16B ✓, IV 12B ✓, key 32B ✓, payload = 2928B ct + 16B tag ✓. Cockpit vault v2 = 3 wraps (primary-52/canon-62/word), each iter 600,000 ✓, salt 16B, IV 12B, 48B wrap-ct; body 19707B ct (GCM).
findings.why: Matches SECURITY.md exactly; GCM-authenticated-decrypt-as-verifier on both gates is the correct pattern (no timing-compare needed).
findings.fix: None.

findings.what: Password handling verified: zero localStorage/sessionStorage/cookie/IndexedDB anywhere (grep-verified, only doc comments); console fetches same-origin only (connect-src 'self', observed assets only per agent-3d's live network log); password is TextEncoder'd in-memory, never sent, cleared from the field on success; cockpit auto-locks at 15 min and clears state; signing is posting-authority-only with a structural block on stale/not-on-chain accounts (getPostingPriv), low-s ECDSA with random k from crypto.getRandomValues; broadcast sends signed tx only — no key material ever leaves the tab.
findings.why: The owner's core demand (password gate, no exposed tokens) is honored in code, not just in docs.
findings.fix: None.

findings.what: The network board is the hygiene gold standard: CSP default-src 'none' with script-src/style-src 'self', form-action 'none', base-uri 'none'; zero innerHTML/eval — DOM built exclusively via createElement/textContent; probe fetches public unauthenticated sources with 10s timeouts, fail-soft per source, atomic tmp+rename writes, tail-128 log. One functional (non-security) note: app.js:226 reads f.witness while network-probe.mjs writes witness_row, and app.js:229 reads sources.note while the probe writes notes — the witness panel will show 'לא-זמין' until the field names converge.
findings.why: Shows the desired security posture is repeatable across agents; the field mismatch is worth a one-line heads-up to agent-3b before it ships.
findings.fix: Align witness_row↔witness and notes↔note field names (functional, not security).

findings.what: Credential handling in boot is sound: token from env or gitignored upload/pat.env; only its length is printed; flows via git credential-helper (never embedded in a clone URL, honoring the repo's own cred-url leak-scan law); no curl|bash anywhere — repos are cloned and scripts run from the clone; work dirs are mkdir 700 / mktemp -d 700; extracted secrets land 0600.
findings.why: The highest-privilege script in the repo follows the no-token-in-URL and no-remote-exec rules it was given.
findings.fix: None (the /tmp code-execution aspect is F-M2).
